# ProMIS Neurosciences Licenses Next-Generation TXP1 Brain-Selective Shuttling Technology from Ossianix to Expand PMN310 Franchise and Pipeline


Nov 17, 2026[Download as PDF](https://d1io3yog0oux5.cloudfront.net/_3df3a268711757a7d9b1ac21b935acd3/promisneurosciences/news/2026-11-17_ProMIS_Neurosciences_Licenses_Next_Generation_280.pdf)


*TXP1 selectively increased antibody delivery to the brain by more than 65-fold in preclinical studies conducted by Ossianix*


*License supports lifecycle management of the PMN310 franchise, with options to extend TXP1 to ProMIS’s Parkinson’s and ALS programs*


**Cambridge, Massachusetts, Nov. 17, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) --** ProMIS Neurosciences Inc. (Nasdaq: PMN), a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing antibodies that selectively target toxic misfolded proteins in neurodegenerative diseases, today announced that it has entered into a license agreement with Ossianix, Inc. for TXP1, a next-generation brain-selective shuttling technology targeting transferrin receptor 1 (TfR1). The agreement provides ProMIS rights to use TXP1 with PMN310, its lead antibody for Alzheimer’s disease (AD), and options to apply the technology to its Parkinson’s disease (PD) and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) programs.


“This partnership is in support of the long-term value of our pipeline. Our ongoing efforts with PMN310 are unaffected by this agreement and we remain committed to advancing it as an intravenous (IV) and subcutaneous product, subject to upcoming data,” said Neil Warma, President and Chief Executive Officer of ProMIS Neurosciences. “We believe TXP1 is among the most compelling TfR1 shuttles in development. Pairing it with antibodies that are selective for toxic misfolded proteins may provide a path to a second-generation PMN310 in AD with a more convenient subcutaneous dosing schedule and lower cost of goods and to next-generation candidates in our pipeline.”


TXP1 is built on a deimmunized, single-domain VNAR antibody scaffold that is significantly smaller than a conventional antibody. In preclinical studies reported by Ossianix, including studies in non-human primates, TXP1 increased delivery of a therapeutic antibody to the brain by more than 65-fold, with no accumulation observed in the liver, spleen, lung, kidney, bone marrow, heart or muscle. Ossianix has also reported a favorable PK profile with prolonged brain exposure, binding that does not compete with transferrin, and minimal impact on reticulocyte levels, an effect that has been reported with some TfR1-targeting approaches. Based on these preclinical data, ProMIS believes TXP1 has a differentiated profile among TfR1-based shuttles.


“We are proud to partner with ProMIS and see this agreement as strong validation of TXP1’s profile as a next-generation TfR1-targeting delivery technology,” said Frank Walsh, CEO of Ossianix. “By pairing our deimmunized VNAR platform—which binds a unique epitope—with ProMIS’s selective antibodies, we see a compelling opportunity to enable more convenient dosing across Alzheimer’s and expand into additional neurodegenerative programs.”


Under the terms of the agreement, Ossianix will receive an upfront payment and is eligible to receive development, regulatory and commercial milestone payments, as well as royalties on global net sales. ProMIS also holds options to apply TXP1 to PMN442, its antibody targeting alpha-synuclein (implicated in Parkinson’s disease and dementia with Lewy bodies), and PMN267, its antibody targeting TDP-43 (implicated in ALS and frontotemporal dementia). ProMIS intends to fund its short-term obligations under the agreement from existing cash resources and does not expect the agreement to change its previously disclosed cash runway through 2027.


Destum Partners served as transaction advisor to Ossianix.


**About ProMIS Neurosciences Inc.**


ProMIS Neurosciences is a clinical-stage biotechnology company committed to the discovery and development of therapeutic antibodies and vaccines selective for toxic oligomers associated with the development and progression of neurodegenerative and other misfolded protein diseases. The Company’s proprietary target discovery engine, EpiSelect™, has been shown to predict novel targets known as Disease Specific Epitopes (DSEs) on the molecular surface of misfolded proteins that cause neurodegenerative and other misfolded protein diseases, including Alzheimer’s disease (AD), amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), frontotemporal dementia (FTD), Parkinson’s disease (PD), and dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB). ProMIS has offices in Cambridge, Massachusetts (USA) and Toronto, Ontario (CAN).


**About PMN310**


PMN310, the Company’s lead product candidate for the treatment of AD, is a humanized IgG1 monoclonal antibody designed to selectively target toxic oligomers while avoiding plaque, thereby potentially reducing or eliminating amyloid-related imaging abnormalities (ARIA) liability. PMN310 was granted Fast Track designation by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration in July 2025 and is being evaluated in PRECISE-AD (NCT06750432), a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 1b study in patients with mild cognitive impairment due to AD or mild AD.


**About Ossianix, Inc.**


Ossianix is a privately held drug discovery and development company pioneering a new generation of brain-selective delivery technologies based on naturally occurring single-domain antibodies known as VNARs. Ossianix is headquartered in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, with research laboratories in Stevenage, United Kingdom.
